objective: Frozen computation: for each recurrent round of the ten, test whether the newest-ancestor, most-chains and fewest-chains relations are perfect matchings of round t with rounds t - 2 and t - 3, and whether the full spine relation's perfect matching is unique.
status: Supported 2026-11-19 (5 of 5 held; refereed R1, confirmed): on 204 recurrent rounds of the ten y^2(1+y) break-shape eddies, the newest-ancestor rule fails by count, most chains keeps only depth-3 ancestors and fails likewise (with collisions in 10 of 10 by round 13), fewest chains leaves most junctions tied, and no pair is forced (forced share 0 at every round); a degree-preserving shuffle of the spine relation still has a perfect pairing (30 of 30).
title: Three spine rules on the ten plastic-number eddies
